hero.headline: Multiple lanes reopen on I-95 South in Delray Beach after crash with injuries
hero.teaser: Four lanes of I-95 South in Delray Beach were blocked Thursday morning after a crash just before the Atlantic Avenue exit resulted in injuries.
hero.body:
Multiple lanes of I-95 South in Delray Beach were blocked due to a crash Thursday morning. The accident occurred at around 6 a.m. just before the Atlantic Avenue exit, prompting four lanes to shut down. There were injuries as a result of the crash, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

As of 6:25 a.m., all lanes are back open. The Florida Highway Patrol responded to the scene to investigate the crash and clear the roadway for morning commuters.

cards.headline: Driver crashes into Hobe Sound water plant pipe, flees scene; hundreds lose service
cards.teaser: A driver crashed into a large pipe at the Hobe Sound/Osprey Water Plant and fled the scene Wednesday night, leaving hundreds of homes without water service or a.
cards.body:
A driver crashed into a large pipe at the Hobe Sound/Osprey Water Plant and fled the scene Wednesday night, leaving hundreds of homes without water service or adequate water pressure, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The crash occurred at around 9 p.m. Eliuvar Garza, 24, of Stuart has been charged with leaving the scene of a crash with property damage, driving with a suspended license with knowledge, failure to use due care, and failure to stop at a stop sign. Garza was located when a family member brought him into the hospital for injuries associated with the crash. A witness said the individual repeatedly stated "I messed up" before running from the scene.

Water services are now fully restored in the area, according to the South Martin Regional Utility. SMRU posted an advisory on its website stating that customers affected by the water shortage should boil their water for three minutes before using it. The SMRU emergency response team has restored water to all customers affected by the incident. The boil water warning is in effect until further notice. Hobe Sound residents with questions about their water service should contact the water company directly.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds committee launches $20 million statewide ad campaign ahead of Florida GOP primary
cards.teaser: Friends of Byron Donalds is launching a $20 million statewide advertising buy beginning Tuesday, June 30, and running through Primary Day on August 18.
cards.body:
Friends of Byron Donalds is launching a $20 million statewide advertising buy beginning Tuesday, June 30, and running through Primary Day on August 18. The campaign spans cable, broadcast, streaming and radio across every major media market in Florida, representing the largest single media investment the committee has made. Ryan Smith, Chair of Friends of Byron Donalds PAC, said the buy aims to tell Floridians that Donalds is the only governor candidate of either party who will fight to lower the cost of living, hold government accountable for spending, and protect the health and safety of families.

The Naples Republican, who represents Florida's 19th Congressional District, has led the GOP field throughout the cycle with surveys showing him ahead of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, investor James Fishback and former House Speaker Paul Renner by margins as wide as 40-plus points. One poll showed his support among likely Primary voters at 54 percent. Donalds' political operation has raised more than $81 million from over 35,000 donors and carried roughly $65 million in the bank into mid-June. President Donald Trump backed Donalds in February 2025, followed by endorsements from Donald Trump Jr., Elon Musk, late Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, U.S. Sen. Rick Scott, the majority of Florida sheriffs, and dozens of state legislators and conservative leaders. The Primary Election is August 18, with the General Election in November.

cards.headline: Federal report reveals structural problems started weeks before Surfside condo collapse
cards.teaser: Federal investigators concluded the problem that led to the deadly Surfside condo collapse five years ago started three weeks before the June 24, 2021 disaster that killed 98 people.
cards.body:
Five years after the 12-story Champlain Towers South crumbled in Surfside on June 24, 2021, federal investigators have identified when structural failure began. The National Institute of Standards and Technology released a technical report Monday concluding the problem started three weeks before the collapse, when two connectors between garage columns and the pool deck failed. This failure caused cracks to grow and shifted loads to columns not engineered to support them. The disaster killed 98 people. Investigators attributed the failure to two factors: severe and widespread deviations in the building's original structural design and standards of the day, and deviations in construction from the design drawings. Federal investigators are now completing their final report, which will include recommendations for changes to standards, codes and practices to improve building safety.

The collapse exposed Florida's history of lax building oversight and prompted swift legislative action. State lawmakers passed new laws requiring more stringent building regulations and mandates for structural inspections. Condominiums must now maintain minimum reserve funding for structural upkeep. However, the reforms sparked controversy as higher HOA fees and assessments drove many residents away from condo living. Lawmakers subsequently made additional adjustments to ease the financial burden on residents.

hero.headline: Belle Glade's West Technical Education Center offers trade certifications in culinary, welding, carpentry
hero.teaser: West Technical Education Center in Belle Glade provides trade training programs and certifications for high school students and adults seeking work in the area.
hero.body:
West Technical Education Center in Belle Glade provides training programs designed to prepare both high school students and adults for careers in skilled trades. The center offers certifications in culinary arts, welding, carpentry and several other trade fields that lead directly to employment opportunities. According to Adrian Dowdell with the education center, "West Tech is really appropriate for high school students and adults looking to learn a trade and get certifications that lead to work."

The center recently brought attention to its programs by participating in a community event at the Belle Glade library. Staff members displayed a large truck at the gathering to engage with residents and share information about the various training options available. The outreach effort was part of a broader community initiative, with WPTV Morning Anchor Ashley Glass connecting with the education center to highlight their mission and available programs.

A key part of West Technical Education Center's approach involves partnering with local businesses and community organizations. These partnerships help connect graduates with employment opportunities throughout Belle Glade and the surrounding region. By working closely with employers, the center ensures that its training programs align with actual job market needs and that students have pathways to secure positions after completing their certifications.

The education center's presence at community events demonstrates its commitment to raising awareness about trade training opportunities. For residents interested in learning more about the programs or exploring whether a trade certification might be right for them, the center actively seeks to connect with community members. West Technical Education Center serves as a resource for those looking to develop practical skills and enter the workforce quickly through certified training in high-demand trades.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County School District begins layoffs as 76 media clerks lose jobs, hundreds more cuts expected
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County has confirmed that layoffs have started, with 76 media clerks already out of work.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County has confirmed that layoffs have started, with 76 media clerks already out of work. The cuts are designed to offset a drop in student enrollment and to fund teacher pay raises approved in April. According to the district's April projections, 192 teachers, 19 administrators, and 43 office assistants could be laid off next.

Tami Slater, a media clerk at Sunset Palms Elementary, received a phone call Monday informing her that her position had been eliminated after 25 years with the district. Media clerks often support media specialists and manage as many as two classes at a time, nearly 60 kids. Slater had planned to work five to eight more years before retirement. She helped students find books, assisted in the cafeteria, and worked during pick-up and drop-off. Though she supported the teacher pay raises, she never thought they could cost her job. School Board Member Gloria Branch warned about this trade-off when the raises were approved in April. The district says it will try to re-employ affected workers in other positions. Slater has already applied for an available role, but it offers lower pay and fewer hours.

cards.headline: Thunderstorms topple trees, damage property across Royal Palm Beach and Wellington
cards.teaser: Strong storms Wednesday night uprooted trees, twisted fences and knocked down light poles in Royal Palm Beach and Wellington neighborhoods.
cards.body:
Strong thunderstorms swept through Royal Palm Beach and Wellington Wednesday night, toppling trees, twisting fences and knocking down light poles across both communities. A large tree was uprooted and fell into the road in one Royal Palm Beach neighborhood, blocking traffic. Firefighters responded and pulled the tree from the road so neighbors could clear it. Hail pelted cars, lightning struck close to residents and strong winds caused widespread damage throughout the area.

Seven-year-old Danny Jaworski was home with his grandmother when the storm hit. "I heard a cracking sound and then a boom," Danny said as he watched the massive tree come down in front of a car driving down their street. Danny's mother, Leslie Jaworski, owns the home, which had been named the neighborhood's Home of the Month. She was at work when the storm hit and came home to find firefighters already on scene working to clear the tree. "I was grateful that the tree didn't go this way and land on my roof, because I've heard horror stories of that. I was grateful that the traffic was able to get through," Leslie said. "I know it could definitely be worse."

cards.headline: Speeding Jeep triggers eight-vehicle pileup on Dixie Highway in Lantana, killing 67-year-old man
cards.teaser: Jose Bedoya, 67, was killed Tuesday when a speeding Jeep Wrangler struck a truck near Ocean Avenue and Dixie Highway, then slammed into stopped traffic.
cards.body:
A Jeep Wrangler speeding along Dixie Highway in Lantana struck a truck near Ocean Avenue on Tuesday, fled the scene, then slammed into stopped traffic, causing an eight-vehicle pileup. Jose Bedoya, 67, was killed in the crash. Two people were transported via trauma hawk from the scene. Surveillance video obtained by WPTV captured the moments before the deadly collision.

Sal Perna, who owns a car rental business near the scene, witnessed the Jeep traveling at extreme speeds. Perna estimated the vehicle was going approximately 100 mph. He said the scale of destruction was unlike anything he had seen in his 11 years at the location, with vehicles so damaged they were unrecognizable. Perna is calling for increased police presence on Dixie Highway, stating that dangerous driving occurs daily. He noted seeing drivers regularly traveling at 50, 60, and 70 mph on the road. Investigators confirmed the case remains an ongoing, active investigation.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves $1.3 million water treatment plan for Sawgrass Lakes community
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie city council approved funding Monday for a three-year treatment plan using a solution called trymarine to address water quality issues in the Sawgrass Lakes community after a fish kill wiped out around 1,100 fish.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie city council approved funding Monday for a $1.3 million three-year treatment plan using trymarine to address water quality issues in the Sawgrass Lakes community. The action follows a fish kill weeks earlier that killed approximately 1,100 fish in the stormwater tract. The city will continue using vendor SOLitutde to conduct the treatment and test water quality. Kevin Matyjaszek, utility systems director for Port St. Lucie, said the stormwater tract has muck and sediment issues that lower oxygen levels and water quality, making it susceptible to algae growth. Matyjaszek said the city wants to ensure the treatment approach is correct and the chemistry is right.

Bob Shonce, HOA president of North Panther Trace at Sawgrass Lakes, said he and other neighbors have observed water quality changes for over five years. In March, city staff listened to Shonce and other neighbors' concerns, and most of the community voted to try trymarine. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, cautioned that while trymarine may help reduce sediment in the water, it may not address where the muck originates. Moir said the city needs to look at the underlying issue, noting that if nutrient supply continues, the problem will recur.

cards.headline: South Fork High School football team begins summer workouts under new head coach
cards.teaser: South Fork High School's football team in Stuart is preparing for the upcoming fall season under new head coach Eric Kresser, who previously coached at The Benjamin School.
cards.body:
South Fork High School's football team is back in summer workouts in Stuart as the Bulldogs prepare for the upcoming fall season under new head coach Eric Kresser. Kresser, who previously served as The Benjamin School head coach, has taken over the program. The team is fully into summer conditioning and participating in 7 on 7 tournaments.

Kresser is looking to turn things around for a program that hasn't had a winning season since 2015. Senior Jaahad Henry said the team is energized heading into the season and believes the new coaching staff is the key to a quick turnaround. "We have a lot of great guys out here," Henry said. "We have some great coaches, a lot of great coaches and we're going to have a great season this year." The Bulldogs are set to begin the season in August.

cards.headline: Jupiter Medical Center breaks ground on new hospital in western Palm Beach Gardens
cards.teaser: Jupiter Medical Center held a groundbreaking ceremony Wednesday for a new hospital in the Avenir community off Northlake Boulevard in western Palm Beach Gardens, expected to open in early 2028.
cards.body:
A new Jupiter Medical Center hospital is coming to western Palm Beach Gardens, with a groundbreaking ceremony Wednesday marking the start of construction in the Avenir community off Northlake Boulevard. The facility, expected to open in early 2028, will serve approximately 40,000 residents in the immediate vicinity. JMC President and CEO Dr. Amit Rastogi said the expansion is part of the organization's mission to reach underserved areas. The neighborhood hospital will have 29 inpatient beds, 24-hour emergency services and four operating rooms.

Palm Beach Gardens Mayor Dana Middleton, who lives in the western part of the city, said the new hospital addresses concerns that became especially clear after construction last summer shut down Northlake Boulevard at the Beeline Highway. Residents' top concern was how they would access the hospital and doctors during the closure. Palm Beach North Chamber President Noel Martinez said access to healthcare is a key factor businesses consider when evaluating a region, along with schools and transportation. The new JMC facility is the latest development in a period of rapid growth for area medical facilities. Miller Medical Center opened in April in Palm Beach Gardens and is the first full-service hospital to open in the area since 1979. At the beginning of the year, Jupiter Medical Center opened a new 92-bed Patient Care Tower.

cards.body:
Breeze Airways announced Wednesday five new routes from Vero Beach Regional Airport with one-way fares starting at $79. Nonstop flights to Atlantic City operate Mondays and Fridays starting October 2 from $89 one way. Nonstop service to Baltimore runs Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays beginning October 1 from $79 one way. Nonstop flights to Trenton operate Wednesdays and Saturdays starting September 30 from $89 one way, with service switching to Thursdays and Sundays beginning January 7.

The airline also offers one-stop, no-change-of-plane BreezeThru service to Burlington, Vermont on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays starting October 4, and to Provo, Utah on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays starting October 2. Breeze, which started operations in 2021, currently operates more than 300 year-round and seasonal routes to 91 cities in the United States, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean. Vero Beach Regional Airport has increased flight options to serve the Treasure Coast's growing population. JetBlue began service to Boston and New York's JFK airports in December, and American Airlines began service to Charlotte in February.

Stephanie Berry, the facility manager, emphasizes the importance of these lessons for water safety in the community. Over the past one to two years, there have been a couple of drownings in Belle Glade, and Berry said swim lessons are critical to build water competency.

According to the Drowning Prevention Coalition of Palm Beach County, 41 children died from 2020 to 2024, with pools being one of the most deadly areas. Other locations include canals, lakes, ponds, the Intracoastal Waterway and the ocean. Reynaldo Perez Jr., a father of two, signed his children up for the free lessons because they live in Florida and are surrounded by water. Some parents never learned how to swim themselves, so they are now learning alongside their children. The program is offered year-round, with registration available in person every other Saturday starting at 8:30 a.m. Lessons are held Tuesdays through Fridays for two weeks.

cards.headline: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League urges pet owners to create hurricane disaster plans with emergency kits
cards.teaser: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is urging South Florida residents to prepare disaster plans for pets before the next hurricane, including microchips, emergency kits and safe room drills.
cards.body:
Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is urging South Florida residents to create a disaster plan for their pets before hurricane season intensifies. Dr. Alyssa Comroe, CEO of Peggy Adams, emphasized that the safest place for pets during a hurricane is alongside their owners. The shelter's expert team recommends microchipping pets and ensuring they wear collars with current identification. Pet owners should introduce their animals to a designated safe room, such as a walk-in closet or downstairs bathroom, and conduct practice runs before a storm arrives.

The organization advises preparing a pet emergency kit containing a three-day supply of food and water in airtight containers, bowls, a sturdy carrier, bedding, towels, medications for two weeks, vaccination records, first-aid supplies, litter and box for cats, leashes, harnesses, cool packs, wipes, waste bags, and multiple forms of visible ID. Pet owners should keep a printed list of local pet-friendly shelters and hotels accessible and maintain recent photos of pets, ideally with their owner, for identification if separated. Peggy Adams also recommends conducting hurricane drills that include pets' daily routines such as feeding, drinking water, and resting inside the safe room. Florida's hurricane season runs June through November. The organization notes that proper storm preparation reduces risk during evacuations, while year-round heat safety measures including water enrichment, shade, and limiting midday walks help protect pets.

cards.headline: Strong storms topple trees and damage fences in Royal Palm Beach and Wellington neighborhoods
cards.teaser: Thunderstorms swept through Royal Palm Beach and Wellington Wednesday night, uprooting a large tree that blocked a street and causing damage to fences and light poles across both communities.
cards.body:
Strong thunderstorms swept through Royal Palm Beach and Wellington Wednesday night, toppling trees, twisting fences and knocking down light poles across both communities. A large tree was uprooted and fell into the road in one Royal Palm Beach neighborhood, blocking traffic. Firefighters responded and pulled the tree from the road so neighbors could clear it. Hail pelted cars, lightning struck close to residents and strong winds caused widespread damage throughout the area.

Seven-year-old Danny Jaworski was home with his grandmother when the storm hit. "I heard a cracking sound and then a boom," Danny said as the massive tree came down in front of a car driving down their street. Danny's mother, Leslie Jaworski, owns the home, which had been named the neighborhood's Home of the Month. She was at work when the storm hit and came home to find firefighters already on scene. "I was grateful that the tree didn't go this way and land on my roof, because I've heard horror stories of that," Leslie said. "I'm a new homeowner, so it does kind of make me worried about future storms and what can happen," she added.

hero.headline: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League urges hurricane prep for pets with microchips, emergency kits
hero.teaser: The West Palm Beach animal shelter is urging South Florida residents to create disaster plans for pets before the next storm hits during hurricane season.
hero.body:
As hurricane season intensifies across South Florida, Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is encouraging residents to develop comprehensive disaster plans for their pets. Dr. Alyssa Comroe, CEO of Peggy Adams, emphasizes that pets are safest during hurricanes when they stay with their owners. The organization's expert team has outlined essential preparation steps that every pet owner should take before the next storm arrives.

The shelter recommends several critical safety measures starting with identification. Pets should wear collars with current ID tags and have updated microchips registered with accurate contact information. Equally important is preparing pets mentally for storms by introducing them to a designated safe room well in advance. This space might be a walk-in closet or downstairs bathroom. Practice runs inside the safe room before hurricane season arrives help reduce stress and confusion when an actual storm threatens.

Pet owners need to assemble a comprehensive emergency kit containing supplies for at least three days. The kit should include food and water stored in airtight containers, bowls, a sturdy carrier, bedding, towels, medications for two weeks, vaccination records, and first-aid supplies. Cat owners should add litter and a litter box. The kit should also contain leashes, harnesses, cool packs, wipes, waste bags, and multiple forms of visible identification. Keeping a printed list of local pet-friendly shelters and hotels in an easily accessible location ensures pet owners know where to go if evacuation becomes necessary. Recent photos of pets, ideally showing them with their owners, are invaluable for identification if pets become separated during the chaos of a storm.

The shelter also recommends conducting hurricane drills that incorporate pets' normal daily routines, including feeding, water access, and rest periods inside the safe room. These practice sessions help maximize comfort when an actual emergency occurs. Pet owners should remember that Florida's hurricane season runs from June through November, a period that coincides with extreme summer heat. Beyond storm preparation, year-round heat safety measures such as providing water enrichment, adequate shade, and avoiding midday walks help protect pets throughout the season. Taking time to prepare now significantly reduces risks for pets during evacuations and emergency situations.

cards.headline: Florida Mango Festival showcases 75 vendors, rare varieties in West Palm Beach Saturday
cards.teaser: The Florida Mango Festival will take place Saturday, June 27, at the Palm Beach County Convention Center at 650 Okeechobee Boulevard in West Palm Beach.
cards.body:
The Florida Mango Festival will take place Saturday, June 27, at the Palm Beach County Convention Center at 650 Okeechobee Boulevard in West Palm Beach. More than 75 vendors will showcase local mango varieties, grafted trees, tropical fruits, and mango-themed products in the indoor, air-conditioned venue. Festival co-organizer Vince Rogers said Florida hosts more than 350 mango varieties, including Fruit Cocktail with sweet, multi-layered flavor; Orange Sherbet offering creamy citrus notes; and Pineapple Pleasure with tropical pineapple undertones. Rogers noted that backyard-grown Tommy Atkins mangoes are much more superior to anything available in stores, and that the varieties extend far beyond what grocery stores typically carry.

Throughout the day, visitors can attend educational talks on home mango growing and grafting techniques. Alex Salazar of Tropical Acres Farms will lead demonstrations offering tips for both beginners and seasoned growers. The festival will also feature an ID Your Mango booth, a scion exchange for online mango community members, and a master display of Florida's diverse mango cultivars. The event begins at 10:30 a.m., with first pick ticket holders entering at 9 a.m. Garage parking is included with tickets but has limited availability. Paid public parking is available nearby north of Okeechobee Boulevard. Tickets and more information are available at floridamangofestival.com.

hero.headline: Lt. Gov. Jay Collins says Ron DeSantis endorsement a matter of when, not if
hero.teaser: Jay Collins says Gov. Ron DeSantis will endorse him for governor when he decides to jump into the race, expressing confidence it's only a matter of time.
hero.body:
Jay Collins believes Governor Ron DeSantis will eventually endorse him in the race to succeed DeSantis as Florida's chief executive. When asked on Fox News Radio whether he wanted to see the governor formally back his appointed lieutenant governor, Collins indicated it's inevitable. "The Governor and I are in a great space. I know where he is, and when he decides to jump into this race, you'll have no doubt that he's in," Collins said. "When he's ready, I'm sure he'll make the appropriate decision."

Collins' campaign is facing significant headwinds in the Republican primary. He trails front-runner Byron Donalds by more than 44 points in average polling. Donalds has built a substantial financial advantage, holding $65 million in campaign funds according to the most recent reports. Collins, by comparison, has roughly $5.5 million on hand after raising less than $68,000 between his campaign account and affiliated committee in a recent period while spending more than $590,000, including $140,000 spent on fundraising consulting.

Collins attempted to draw parallels between his current polling position and DeSantis' performance eight years earlier. He pointed out that DeSantis won the 2018 gubernatorial race against Adam Putnam and cited Rick Scott's 2010 victory over Bill McCollum as evidence that Floridians often reject the apparent frontrunner. However, the comparison is problematic. Collins currently averages 6.5 percent in polls, with results ranging from 1 to 15 percent in surveys conducted since October. In contrast, DeSantis polled at 15 percent in a Florida Chamber survey and 21 percent in an NBC News/Marist survey in 2018. Like Donalds, DeSantis received an endorsement from President Donald Trump, a significant political advantage Collins does not currently possess. Scott, unlike Collins, possessed independent wealth that allowed him to fund his campaign liberally, a crucial difference in both races.

Collins' path to the nomination appears increasingly difficult without a dramatic shift in either his polling or fundraising. The gap between his resources and Donalds' financial capacity continues to widen, and he remains a distant third in most matchups. Collins is betting that DeSantis' endorsement could change the dynamics of the race, much as Trump's backing helped both DeSantis and Donalds in their respective campaigns. For now, the lieutenant governor is publicly expressing confidence that the governor's support will materialize when the time is right.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds committee launches $20 million statewide ad campaign ahead of Florida GOP primary
cards.teaser: Friends of Byron Donalds is launching a $20 million statewide advertising buy beginning Tuesday, June 30, and running through Primary Day on August 18.
cards.body:
Friends of Byron Donalds is launching a $20 million statewide advertising buy beginning Tuesday, June 30, and running through Primary Day on August 18. The campaign spans cable, broadcast, streaming and radio across every major media market in Florida, representing the largest single media investment the committee has made. Ryan Smith, Chair of Friends of Byron Donalds PAC, said the buy aims to tell Floridians that Donalds is the only governor candidate of either party who will fight to lower the cost of living, hold government accountable for spending, and protect the health and safety of families.

The Naples Republican, who represents Florida's 19th Congressional District, has led the GOP field throughout the cycle with surveys showing him ahead of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, investor James Fishback and former House Speaker Paul Renner by margins as wide as 40-plus points. One poll showed his support among likely Primary voters at 54 percent. Donalds' political operation has raised more than $81 million from over 35,000 donors and carried roughly $65 million in the bank into mid-June. President Donald Trump backed Donalds in February 2025, followed by endorsements from Donald Trump Jr., Elon Musk, late Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, U.S. Sen. Rick Scott, the majority of Florida sheriffs, and dozens of state legislators and conservative leaders. The Primary Election is August 18, with the General Election in November.

cards.headline: Navy reserve officer Dan Green secures law enforcement and veteran endorsements in Congressional District 9 race
cards.teaser: Dan Green, a Vero Beach Republican and reserve Navy officer, has rolled out a roster of endorsements from law enforcement, fellow veterans and Treasure Coast officials in his campaign for Florida's redrawn 9th Congressional District.
cards.body:
Vero Beach Republican and Navy reserve officer Dan Green has secured endorsements from prominent law enforcement and military figures in his bid for Florida's 9th Congressional District. Brevard County Sheriff Wayne Ivey said endorsing Green for Congress is an easy choice, noting he will stand with President Trump to keep communities safe, protect the military and grow the economy. Danny Burgess, an Army reservist and former head of the Florida Department of Veterans Affairs, said Floridians deserve a fighter in Washington who will stand with President Trump and put families first. Retired Navy SEAL Mark Donald, a recipient of the Navy Cross, Silver Star, Bronze Star with V and Purple Heart who served alongside Green, endorsed him as a man of honesty, understanding and intelligence focused on fixing issues.

Under the new congressional map Gov. Ron DeSantis signed in May, Congressional District 9 was reshaped from a Democratic-leaning Central Florida seat into Republican turf that backed President Donald Trump with roughly 58 percent of the vote. The district now runs from the Orlando exurbs in Orange, Osceola and Polk counties south through the middle of the state to take in Indian River, Okeechobee, Highlands and Glades counties. The redistricting turned a seat held by Democratic U.S. Rep. Darren Soto into a magnet for Republican candidates. Green is competing in an Aug. 18 GOP Primary that also includes Ben Butler, Marcus Carter, Thomas Chalifoux Jr., Jorge Martinez, Steve Rance and Justin Story.

cards.headline: Rick Scott says he invited Trump to Senate lunch that flipped Iran War Powers vote
cards.teaser: U.S. Sen. Rick Scott says he invited President Donald Trump to a Wednesday Senate policy lunch, where Trump's lobbying convinced Republicans to flip their votes on an Iran War Powers resolution.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans reversed their position on a measure that would have required President Donald Trump to withdraw troops from the Persian Gulf, potentially after Rick Scott invited Trump to a weekly Senate lunch. Scott told Fox and Friends that he extended the Friday invitation to the Wednesday policy lunch he runs. When Trump arrived, Scott recounted that the President said, "What the hell are you guys doing? I'm in the middle of a negotiation, trying to bring Iran to the table, and you guys say we have to withdraw troops."

Scott said Trump was furious with senators who voted for the measure while he attempted to negotiate with Iran. "It was a foolish vote for the people that said, 'Oh, no, we have to withdraw our troops' when we watch what President Trump's trying to do to preserve American lives, and bring peace around the world," Scott added. Bill Cassidy, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul originally voted for H.J. Res. 86, a House-approved measure urging a defensive posture in the conflict, giving the resolution a 50-46 Senate advantage. Following Trump's intervention, Cassidy flipped his vote and Paul voted present, while Collins and Murkowski maintained their positions. With two additional Republicans voting against the resolution who were absent the previous day, the outcome shifted to 47-50-1.

cards.headline: Retired Army general Leela Gray adds Ted Lieu endorsement in Congressional District 13 race
cards.teaser: Democratic candidate Leela Gray announced the endorsement of U.S. Rep. Ted Lieu, the California Democrat who serves as Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus, in her campaign for Florida's 13th Congressional District.
cards.body:
Retired Army Brigadier General Leela Gray announced the endorsement of U.S. Rep. Ted Lieu, a California Democrat and Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus, in her bid for Florida's 13th Congressional District. Lieu, who spent more than two decades in the Air Force and retired as a colonel in the Judge Advocate General's Corps, said the country needs leaders who can cut through chaos and get things done. He praised Gray's career, which was grounded in the principles of getting the job done and taking care of people. Gray characterized Lieu's backing as a marker of credibility, noting that he is a veteran, prosecutor and one of the most effective members of Congress on holding people accountable.

Gray faces an uphill battle in a district redrawn by Gov. Ron DeSantis that no longer favors Democrats. The new congressional map, signed in May, keeps the bulk of Pinellas County but carved out the urban core of St. Petersburg and pushed lines north toward New Port Richey, swapping in more Republican territory. The redrawn district backed President Donald Trump 56 percent to 43 percent in 2024. Gray raised more than $561,000 in under two months after launching her campaign, and an internal poll put her in a statistical tie with two-term Republican U.S. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, trailing 41 percent to 39 percent.

cards.headline: Rep. Jared Moskowitz hosts fourth annual Sneaker Day on Capitol Hill
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Jared Moskowitz, the Parkland Democrat, is hosting the fourth annual Sneaker Day on the Hill where lawmakers from all sides can stand together.
cards.body:
Rep. Jared Moskowitz, a Parkland Democrat, is hosting the fourth annual "Sneaker Day on the Hill," an event where lawmakers from both parties can gather to celebrate sneaker culture. "As the Sneaker of the House, I'm excited to host our fourth annual celebration of everything that makes sneaker culture great," Moskowitz posted on X, noting it is "one of the few things that gets both sides of the aisle laced up." The event spotlights sneaker designers and business leaders through panel remarks from SOLEcial Studies CommUNITY Academy co-founder Sean Williams and Pensole Footwear Design Academy founder D'Wayne Edwards, who will discuss how footwear can lead to career paths.

Rep. Sharice Davids, a Kansas Democrat, is co-hosting the event with other participating members of Congress. This year's celebration will showcase cleats and gear connected to the World Cup, which is being hosted in the United States, including games in Miami. Moskowitz founded the Congressional Sneaker Caucus during his first year in Congress and currently co-chairs it with U.S. Rep. Wesley Hunt, a Texas Republican. Other Florida members include Democratic U.S. Reps. Maxwell Frost, Darren Soto and Frederica Wilson. Moskowitz hosted the first Sneaker Day on June 21, 2023.

cards.headline: Lincoln Project launches ad series contrasting Abraham Lincoln with Donald Trump
cards.teaser: The anti-Donald Trump Lincoln Project is using the Great American State Fair to show how the current President doesn't measure up to Abraham Lincoln, launching its first in a series of ads spotlighting the 16th president.
cards.body:
The Lincoln Project is launching a series of ads at the Great American State Fair comparing Abraham Lincoln to Donald Trump. The first ad focuses on Lincoln's 1858 speech accepting the Republican Senate nomination from Illinois, arguing that a nation cannot be half one thing and half another and survive. The spot contends that Lincoln was unique in declaring slavery wrong, and a narrator draws parallels to today's divide between democracy and autocracy, and rule of law versus rule of one man. Tessa Gould, Lincoln Project Executive Director, contrasts Lincoln's reinvigoration of American liberty, destruction of slavery, and moral leadership with Trump's alleged dismantling of American success.

The campaign includes several additional spots rolling out over coming weeks. "Better Angels," airing Friday, examines Lincoln's inaugural speech as an inflection point offering reconciliation. "Trump" contrasts Lincoln's wartime building record with the current President's peacetime dismantling. "Suckers and Losers," releasing July 2, explores the contrast between a President who wept for the fallen and one who called them suckers, described as the emotional gut punch of the series. "Character" releases July 4 and ties Lincoln quotes to America's 250th anniversary. Forthcoming podcasts will feature political consultant emeritus James Carville and lawyer Jeffrey Toobin as guests.

hero.headline: West Technical Education Center offers trade certifications to Belle Glade residents
hero.teaser: West Technical Education Center in Belle Glade provides training programs in culinary, welding, carpentry and other trades to help high school students and adults get certified and find work.
hero.body:
West Technical Education Center in Belle Glade is working to connect residents with job training opportunities through a variety of specialized programs. The center recently promoted its offerings at a community event held at the Belle Glade library, where staff members engaged with potential students interested in learning trades. According to Adrian Dowdell with the education center, the programs available include culinary arts, welding, and carpentry, among other options designed to prepare people for careers in the trades.

The center serves both high school students and adults who are looking to gain practical skills and earn certifications that can lead directly to employment. Dowdell noted that "West Tech is really appropriate for high school students and adults looking to learn a trade and get certifications that lead to work." This dual focus allows the center to reach different populations in the community who may be interested in pursuing alternative career paths to traditional four-year college programs.

A key aspect of West Technical Education Center's approach involves building strong relationships with local organizations and businesses. The center actively works with community and business partners to help graduates find employment opportunities in Belle Glade and the surrounding communities. This partnership model helps ensure that the training programs remain aligned with actual job market demands and that students have clear pathways to positions after completing their certifications.

The center's presence at the library event demonstrates its commitment to raising awareness about the opportunities available to residents. By participating in community gatherings like the Let's Hear It meet-up, West Tech is able to directly reach people who may benefit from their programs. For those interested in learning more about the various trade certifications and training options available, the center remains active in promoting its mission to help Belle Glade residents develop job-ready skills and advance their careers through hands-on technical education.

cards.headline: Stuart man arrested after crashing into Hobe Sound water plant, leaving hundreds without service
cards.teaser: A driver crashed into a large pipe at the Hobe Sound/Osprey Water Plant and fled the scene Wednesday night, leaving hundreds of homes without water service or a.
cards.body:
A driver crashed into a large pipe at the Hobe Sound/Osprey Water Plant and fled the scene Wednesday night, leaving hundreds of homes without water service or adequate water pressure, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The crash occurred around 9 p.m. The sheriff's office located the driver when a family member brought him to the hospital for injuries related to the crash. A witness reported that the driver repeatedly stated "I messed up" before running from the scene.

The driver has been identified as 24-year-old Eliuvar Garza of Stuart. He has been charged with leaving the scene of a crash with property damage, driving with a suspended license with knowledge, failure to use due care, and failure to stop at a stop sign. Water services are now fully restored in the area, according to the South Martin Regional Utility. The utility posted an advisory stating that customers affected by the water shortage should boil their water for three minutes before using it. The boil water warning is in effect until further notice. Hobe Sound residents with questions about their water service should contact the water company directly.

cards.headline: Multiple lanes reopen on I-95 South in Delray Beach after morning crash with injuries
cards.teaser: Four lanes of I-95 South in Delray Beach shut down Thursday morning after a crash that resulted in injuries, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.
cards.body:
Multiple lanes of I-95 South in Delray Beach were blocked due to a crash Thursday morning. The accident occurred at around 6 a.m. just before the Atlantic Avenue exit, prompting four lanes to shut down.

There were injuries as a result of the crash, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. As of 6:25 a.m., all lanes are back open.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves $1.3 million water treatment plan for Sawgrass Lakes stormwater tract
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie city council approved $1.3 million in funding Monday for a three-year water treatment plan to address quality issues in the Sawgrass Lakes community stormwater tract. The city will use vendor SOLitude to apply TryMarine, a treatment solution, and continue testing water quality following a fish kill that wiped out approximately 1,100 fish weeks earlier.

Kevin Matyjaszek, utility systems director for Port St. Lucie, said the stormwater tract has muck and sediment issues that lower oxygen levels and water quality, making it susceptible to algae growth. TryMarine could help reduce the muck and restore oxygen levels, he said. Bob Shonce, HOA president of North Panther Trace at Sawgrass Lakes, said neighbors have observed water changes for over five years. In March, most of the community voted to approve the TryMarine treatment after city staff addressed residents' concerns. However, Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, cautioned that while TryMarine may reduce sediment, it may not address where the muck originates. Moir said the city needs immediate action but also must investigate underlying issues, warning that if an ongoing nutrient supply exists, the problem will recur.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman arrested after allegedly targeting Middle Eastern grocery store

A train strike occurred in Vero Beach Thursday, marking the 10th fatal Brightline incident in the local area. The incident was reported Thursday morning.

This story is developing.

Breeze Airways has added a new route connecting Vero Beach with Atlantic City, expanding air service options for Indian River County residents. The announcement was made Thursday.

cards.headline: Food Pantry of Indian River County sees growing demand as more families seek help
cards.teaser: The Food Pantry of Indian River County is serving more families as need grows across the county.
cards.body:
The Food Pantry of Indian River County is helping more families as demand for food assistance continues to grow. The organization reported an increase in the number of families seeking help.

The food pantry serves residents throughout Indian River County who are facing food insecurity. The organization provides groceries and essential items to families in need.

cards.headline: Royal Palm Beach and Wellington residents clean up after severe storms topple trees and damage property
cards.teaser: Strong thunderstorms swept through Royal Palm Beach and Wellington Wednesday night, toppling trees, twisting fences and knocking down light poles.
cards.body:
Strong thunderstorms swept through Royal Palm Beach and Wellington Wednesday night, toppling trees, twisting fences and knocking down light poles across both communities. Hail pelted cars, lightning struck close to residents and strong winds caused widespread damage throughout the area. A large tree was uprooted and fell into the road in one Royal Palm Beach neighborhood, blocking traffic. Firefighters responded and pulled the tree from the road so neighbors could clear it.

Seven-year-old Danny Jaworski was home with his grandmother when the storm hit. "I heard a cracking sound and then a boom," Danny said as he and his grandmother watched the massive tree come down in front of a car driving down their street. Danny's mother, Leslie Jaworski, owns the home, which had been named the neighborhood's Home of the Month. She was at work when the storm hit and came home to find firefighters already on scene working to clear the tree. "I was grateful that the tree didn't go this way and land on my roof, because I've heard horror stories of that," Leslie said. The experience has left her thinking ahead to future storms. "I'm a new homeowner, so it does kind of make me worried about future storms and what can happen," she said.

cards.headline: Surveillance video shows speeding Jeep before deadly eight-vehicle crash in Lantana kills 67-year-old man
cards.teaser: A Jeep Wrangler speeding along Dixie Highway in Lantana struck a truck before triggering an eight-vehicle pileup that left one man dead and others seriously hurt.
cards.body:
A new video obtained by our newsroom shows the moments before a deadly crash on Dixie Highway in Lantana, capturing a Jeep Wrangler speeding along the road and striking a truck before triggering an eight-vehicle pileup. Sal Perna, who owns a car rental business near the scene, witnessed the crash happen on Tuesday. "I saw this Jeep, 4-door Jeep go by here at I would guesstimate 100 mph," Perna said. Investigators say the Jeep hit a truck near Ocean Avenue and Dixie Highway, fled the scene, then slammed into stopped traffic, causing the pileup. Two people were transported from the scene. Jose Bedoya, 67, was killed in the crash. His son shared a statement remembering his father as "the most hard working selfless person to ever exist" and "a true light in your day if you ever bumped into him." A GoFundMe has been set up to support his family.

Perna said the scale of the destruction was unlike anything he had seen in his 11 years at the location. "I was in shock that there were so many vehicles involved. To the point where they were unrecognizable," Perna said. He is now calling for increased police presence on Dixie Highway, citing dangerous driving as a daily occurrence. "11 years I've been sitting at this desk and every day I see people spending 50, 60, 70 miles an hour. Something needs to be done," Perna said. Investigators confirmed the case remains an ongoing, active investigation.

cards.headline: West Technical Education Center offers trade certifications to Belle Glade residents
cards.teaser: West Technical Education Center in Belle Glade is spreading the word about programs to get people trained and ready to find work.
cards.body:
West Technical Education Center in Belle Glade is offering trade certifications to residents looking to learn new skills and find employment. Adrian Dowdell with the education center said West Tech is appropriate for high school students and adults looking to learn a trade and get certifications that lead to work.

The center offers programs in culinary, welding, carpentry and other trades. West Tech works with community and business partners to help people find work in Belle Glade and surrounding communities. The education center recently set up a truck near a Let's Hear It meet-up at the library in Belle Glade to spread awareness of their programs.
